name: Doorway pec stretch
summary: Forearms on either side of a doorway, step through until the chest stretches.
setup: Stand in a doorway with each forearm on the frame, elbows a little below shoulder height. Step one foot through and lean gently until the chest stretches. Hold, breathing.
why: A doorway hides half the body and the lean is toward the phone; nothing measurable from one angle. Follow the guide and log the hold.
tempo: Ease in over 5 s, hold, ease out.
progression: Elbows higher for the lower chest fibres.
regression: Less lean; one arm at a time.
contraindications: Pain at the front of the shoulder.

faults.label: Shoulders rising
faults.tip: Keep the shoulder blades down and back; the stretch is in the chest, not the neck.

faults.label: Arching the lower back
faults.tip: Brace lightly and lean from the ankles, not the lower back.

faults.label: Elbow too high
faults.tip: Above shoulder height the stretch moves into the front of the joint instead of the chest.

faults.label: Leaning instead of stepping
faults.tip: Take a small step forward rather than throwing the body at the doorway.

guide.surface: A doorway you can lean into safely.
guide.stop: Front-of-shoulder pain or tingling in the hands.
guide.cannotSee: Any of it — the frame hides the arms.

points.t: Forearms on the frame, elbows just below shoulder height.
Lean from the ankles, ribs down, shoulders back.
